comparison_to_previous.basis: Different suite, timing boundaries and CRT configuration; no cross-run performance ratio.

measurement_limits: Single Windows x64 host. Each main case checks all seven repetitions; RSS supplemental suites run one backend per process with three repetitions.
C++ may inline or vectorize numeric/field work; it uses vector/string/unique_ptr ownership rather than Vela object representation and GC.
Async C++ uses the same scheduler and two queued observations per element. Saved-state counters describe Vela continuations, not allocator overhead.
First execution excludes instance construction, includes lazy initialization, and uses benchmark pause/resume accounting.
RSS is a resident snapshot of the full benchmark executable, which links VM and compiler for comparison; it is not peak RSS or an isolated native application's footprint.

Compilation includes source loading, native compilation, wrapper/manifest generation and publication. Link/archive timings use a separate checked arithmetic library and a precompiled C host, directly invoking packaged tools with PATH cleared.
Link/archive measurements exclude compilation and package creation. Package sizes exclude external MSVC/Windows SDK link inputs and compression.
Linux x64/macOS arm64 builds, SDK/license/signing audits and clean-host distribution acceptance remain unverified.

source.description: Revision plus AOT frame/SSA, cold roots, source-position and primitive host-result optimizations; final static-analysis fixes.
source.fingerprint_algorithm: SHA256 of sorted UTF-8 relative path, NUL, binary SHA256(file); .gn/DEPS/BUILD.gn and .cc/.h/.gn/.gni/.py/.vela under base/benchmarks/build/compiler/runtime/tools/vm, plus third_party top-level GN files and Unicode manifest.

comparison_to_previous.basis: Previous entry is Windows x64 on AMD Ryzen 9 7900X; latest is macOS arm64 on Apple M1 Pro. Different machine, target, SDK and host optimization; no cross-run regression ratio.

measurement_limits: Single macOS arm64 host with substantial background load; retain per-case variation when interpreting medians.
C++ arithmetic and field loops can collapse; C++ uses different ownership and unchecked arithmetic. Workload ratios are not per-call language overhead.
Async uses the shared scheduler and two queued observations per element; saved-state counters exclude allocator overhead.
First native execution excludes instantiation, includes lazy initialization and uses pause/resume accounting.
RSS is a resident snapshot of the full comparison process including VM/compiler and prior cases; no per-backend RSS or isolated application footprint is claimed.
Frame bytes and root stores describe the declared LLVM frame and planned safepoints, not the optimized machine stack or dynamic store count.
Compilation/publication metrics are a single build observation, without timing repetitions. Package/link/archive probes were not repeated for this source state.
CPU frequency metadata from Google Benchmark is omitted because sysctl hw.cpufrequency is unavailable; wall timings do not depend on that estimate.
Earlier Windows implementation passed acceptance. These optimization changes have been executed on macOS only; Windows/Linux and macOS clean-host distribution remain unverified.
